## Kronos — Kronos for Defense (open, CC BY 4.0)
How Kronos serves defense — resilient sovereign power from the burner (Aegis) and strategic isotopes from the breeder (tritium, helium-3, 14 MeV neutrons). Public-only; honest about design stage.
Design figures are computed and reproducible; nothing here is economics or an offer of securities.

### Resilient Sovereign Power
- [Aegis and MetroVolt: One Machine, Two Housings](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/metrovolt-and-aegis-shared-machine.html): Aegis (fixed defense installations) and MetroVolt (data centers) are two housings of the same burner, so defense benefits from broader development.
- [Availability Math and the Downtime Budget](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/availability-math-and-downtime-budget.html): Turning availability figures into an annual downtime budget shows exactly how much redundancy a mission-critical installation must carry.
- [Black-Start Capability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/black-start-capability.html): Black-start is the ability to bring an installation's power up from a fully de-energised state without external support; a fusion microgrid must plan for it explicitly.
- [Black-Start of a Base Microgrid](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/black-start-of-a-base-microgrid.html): Restoring a whole base microgrid from cold requires a deliberate sequence in which the fusion unit is brought up last, after a smaller starting source.
- [Blast and EMP Considerations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/blast-and-emp-considerations.html): Blast overpressure and electromagnetic effects threaten controls and power electronics, so a fusion installation must protect its electrical and control systems, not only the reactor.
- [Comparison to Diesel Generation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/comparison-to-diesel-generation.html): Compared with diesel gensets, a fusion installation trades a continuous fuel convoy and large signature for a hard fuel gate and imperfect availability.
- [Comparison to Small Modular Reactors](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/comparison-to-small-modular-reactors.html): Fission microreactors and fusion installations both offer long-interval on-site power; they differ in fuel, waste, signature, and readiness.
- [Continuity During Maintenance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/continuity-during-maintenance.html): Planned maintenance is a predictable outage that must be covered by redundancy so the mission never loses power during servicing.
- [Continuity of Operations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/continuity-of-operations.html): Continuity of operations is the ability to keep mission power flowing through faults, attacks, and maintenance, achieved by layering the fusion unit with storage and redundancy.
- [Cybersecurity of Islanded Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/cybersecurity-of-islanded-power.html): An islanded microgrid's controls are a cyber-physical target; protecting them is as essential to continuity as protecting the reactor.
- [Data-Center Crossover Lessons](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/data-center-crossover-lessons.html): The hyperscale data-center reliability standard that defines the availability gate also offers proven techniques defense power can borrow.
- [Decommissioning and Lifecycle](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/decommissioning-and-lifecycle.html): A fixed installation must be planned for its whole life, including eventual decommissioning of activated structures and management of residual materials.
- [Direct Energy Conversion for Bases](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/direct-energy-conversion-for-bases.html): Direct energy conversion captures charged-particle energy as electricity without a steam cycle, which is attractive for a compact, low-signature installation.
- [Domestic Supply and Sovereignty](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/domestic-supply-and-sovereignty.html): Sovereign power depends on domestic supply of the machine, its fuel, and its critical materials, which the breeder helps provide.
- [Energy Independence for Bases](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/energy-independence-for-bases.html): Energy independence means a fixed installation can generate what it needs without a grid tie or a fuel convoy, within the limits the availability gate imposes.
- [Environmental Siting Considerations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/environmental-siting-considerations.html): A fusion installation must be sited responsibly for water, land, activation, and local impact, consistent with a fixed emplacement's obligations.
- [Fuel Storage vs Fuel Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fuel-storage-vs-fuel-supply.html): On-site helium-3 storage buffers an installation against interruption, but a small stored inventory cannot substitute for a sovereign supply that does not yet exist.
- [Gate: Helium-3 Demand ~400x Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/he3-fuel-supply-gate.html): A single commercial burner unit would demand roughly 400 times the domestic helium-3 supply, so the machine is gated on a fuel that does not exist at terrestrial scale.
- [Gate: Plug Coil Overstressed 3-3.9x](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/plug-coil-stress-gate.html): At the design bore, the burner's high-field plug coil is overstressed by roughly 3 to 3.9 times, making it infeasible as specified without a materials or geometry change.
- [Gate: Plug Regime 166-830x Beyond Devices](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/plug-regime-gate.html): The burner's plug operates in a plasma regime 166 to 830 times beyond any device ever run, so its behaviour cannot be post-dicted from existing data today.
- [Grid Independence from Commercial Utility](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/grid-independence-from-commercial-utility.html): A sovereign installation does not depend on a commercial utility grid, removing a shared vulnerability that off-base power represents.
- [Grid Support and Export When Available](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/grid-support-and-export-when-available.html): An installation that generates its own power can also support or export to the surrounding grid when it is healthy, adding regional resilience.
- [Helium-3 Inventory and Refuelling Logistics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/he3-inventory-and-refueling-logistics.html): Managing a scarce, high-value fuel inventory at an installation is a small but demanding logistics task with strict accountancy and safety requirements.
- [Honest Readiness Summary: Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/honest-readiness-summary-power.html): A single-page summary of what resilient sovereign power from the burner offers, and the four physics gates that stand between the concept and hardware.
- [How the Burner Works: A Primer](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/burner-machine-primer.html): The burner (Aegis / MetroVolt) is a D-3He tandem-mirror generator that converts charged-particle energy directly to electricity, with a small neutron fraction and severe open gates.
- [Hybrid Architecture: Fusion Plus Storage](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/hybrid-power-architecture-fusion-plus-storage.html): Pairing a base-load fusion unit with energy storage and backup generation is what converts an imperfect source into resilient, continuous installation power.
- [Independence Duration and Fuel Interval](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/independence-duration-and-fuel-interval.html): How long a base can run with no external supply is set largely by its on-site fuel interval, a key resilience metric for the burner.
- [Interoperability with Existing Base Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/interoperability-with-existing-base-power.html): A fusion unit must integrate with an installation's existing generation, distribution, and controls rather than requiring a wholesale rebuild.
- [Islanded Microgrid Architecture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/islanded-microgrid-architecture.html): An islanded microgrid lets a base generate, distribute, and control its own power with no reliance on a commercial grid, using the fusion unit as one dispatchable source.
- [Load Following and Transients](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/load-following-and-transients.html): Mission loads change quickly; a base-load fusion unit is paired with storage so the system follows demand without stressing the plasma.
- [Low-Signature Operation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/low-signature-operation.html): A fusion installation aims for a smaller detectable signature than a fuel-fed plant, though it is never signatureless and shielding and cooling still emit.
- [Main Operating Base Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/main-operating-base-power.html): Large fixed bases have continuous, mission-critical demand well suited to a base-load fusion unit inside a redundant, islanded microgrid.
- [Maintenance and Mean-Time-to-Repair](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/maintenance-and-mean-time-to-repair.html): Availability depends as much on how fast a tripped unit is restored as on how often it trips; maintainability is a first-class design requirement.
- [Microgrid Controls and Dispatch](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/microgrid-controls-and-dispatch.html): A microgrid controller decides which sources supply which loads moment to moment, and is what turns imperfect sources into reliable mission power.
- [Mission Assurance and Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/mission-assurance-and-power.html): Mission assurance treats power as a mission-essential function to be guaranteed end to end, aligning power design with the operations it supports.
- [Neutron Fraction and Shielding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-fraction-and-shielding.html): The burner's 5.44% neutron fraction is small but not zero, so a fixed installation still needs shielding, activation management, and a controlled radiation boundary.
- [Operating in a Contested Logistics Environment](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/contested-logistics-environment.html): When supply routes are actively threatened, the ability to generate power on-site becomes a survivability advantage, not merely a convenience.
- [Operator Training and Human Factors](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/operator-training-and-human-factors.html): A novel high-field machine needs trained operators and human-factored controls; skilled people are a resilience factor, not an afterthought.
- [Physical Hardening and Siting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/physical-hardening-and-siting.html): Siting and physical hardening determine how well a fixed fusion installation resists attack and environment, and how its shielding and redundancy are laid out.
- [Power Density and Footprint](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/power-density-and-footprint.html): A compact high-output source with direct energy conversion can reduce the physical footprint of installation power, within siting and shielding limits.
- [Power Quality for Mission-Critical Loads](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/power-quality-and-mission-critical-loads.html): Command, communications, and sensor systems need clean, stable power; the installation must deliver it regardless of what the fusion source is doing.
- [Power for Command and Control](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/power-for-command-and-control.html): Command and control nodes are the highest-priority loads on a base microgrid and are protected by dedicated conditioning, storage, and redundancy.
- [Powering Fixed Forward Sites](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/forward-operating-base-power.html): Fixed forward sites are the hardest logistics case and the strongest motivation for on-site sovereign power, subject to the burner's unresolved gates.
- [Reducing the Attack Surface of Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/reducing-the-attack-surface-of-power.html): On-site generation removes the fuel convoy and grid tie as attack surfaces, while adding a fixed installation and a fuel chain that must be defended.
- [Reducing the Logistics Tail](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/reducing-the-logistics-tail.html): On-site generation shortens the chain of people and vehicles a fixed installation depends on, subject to a different, unresolved fuel supply for fusion.
- [Reliability Growth: FOAK to NOAK](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/reliability-growth-foak-to-noak.html): Availability is expected to improve across the first-of-a-kind, next-of-a-kind, and best-of-a-kind builds, but that improvement is a projection until hardware demonstrates it.
- [Remote and Arctic Installations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/remote-and-arctic-installations.html): Remote and cold-climate sites face the most punishing logistics and environment, raising both the value and the difficulty of on-site fusion power.
- [Resilience Metrics and Definitions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/resilience-metrics-and-definitions.html): Resilience is measurable: availability, reliability, ride-through, restoration time, and independence duration each capture part of it.
- [Resilient Power Design Principles](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/resilient-power-design-principles.html): A short set of principles governs how Kronos designs resilient sovereign power: layered redundancy, honest availability, sovereign fuel, and fail-safe operation.
- [Resilient Sovereign Power: Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/resilient-sovereign-power-overview.html): Kronos studies how a compact fusion generator could supply resilient, self-sufficient power to fixed defense installations, and states plainly the gates that stand between design and hardware.
- [Role in a Diversified Energy Mix](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/role-in-a-diversified-energy-mix.html): Fusion is one element of a diversified installation energy mix, complementing other sources rather than replacing all of them.
- [Safety and Fail-Safe Design](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/safety-and-fail-safe-design.html): A fusion installation near people must be designed to fail safe, with no possibility of runaway and controlled management of its neutron and fuel hazards.
- [Scalability Across Installations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/scalability-across-installations.html): A fleet of standardised burner units across many installations improves reliability growth and supply resilience, but multiplies the fuel demand.
- [Simulation vs Hardware: An Honest Line](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/simulation-vs-hardware-honesty.html): The burner's resilient-power case rests on design and simulation; the line between what is simulated and what is demonstrated is drawn explicitly.
- [Supply-Chain Resilience for Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/supply-chain-resilience-for-power.html): Resilient power needs resilient supply of fuel, spares, and materials; single points of failure upstream undermine on-site generation.
- [Survivability Against Kinetic Threats](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/survivability-against-kinetic-threats.html): Kinetic strikes are addressed by hardening, separation, and redundancy so that damage to one element does not end generation.
- [Survivability and Hardening](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/survivability-and-hardening.html): A fixed fusion installation must be sited and hardened so that generation survives the threats a base faces, from kinetic strikes to environmental extremes.
- [The Availability Gate Explained](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/the-availability-gate-explained.html): Studied burner availability of 0.86-0.995 is 30-100x more downtime than a hyperscale Tier III reference of 0.99982, so a single unit cannot be a sole source today.
- [The Cost in Lives of Fuel Logistics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/cost-in-lives-of-fuel-logistics.html): The dependency on delivered fuel is framed in human risk, not currency, because the people moving and guarding fuel bear the exposure.
- [Thermal Management and Waste Heat](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/thermal-management-and-waste-heat.html): Every power plant rejects waste heat; managing it well serves efficiency, signature, and siting all at once.
- [Thermal and Emissions Signature](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/thermal-and-emissions-signature.html): Waste heat is the dominant residual signature of a fusion installation; managing it is both a survivability and an environmental task.
- [Timeline and Design-Stage Status](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/timeline-and-design-stage-status.html): The breeder leads on a defined timeline; the burner that delivers resilient power is a later machine gated on its own physics.
- [What 'Sovereign' Power Means](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/sovereign-power-definition.html): Sovereign power means the installation's electricity is under national control end to end, from the machine to the fuel, without foreign or commercial dependency.
- [What Net Gain Means for Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/what-net-gain-means-for-power.html): A machine can produce fusion power without producing net electricity; the honest distinction matters for any resilient-power claim.
- [Why Breeder-Bred and Lunar Helium-3 Matter](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/why-breeder-bred-and-lunar-he3-matter.html): The burner's fuel gate is only answerable by a sovereign helium-3 pathway: breeder-bred isotopes now and lunar helium-3 later.
- [Why Fixed Installations, Not Naval](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/why-fixed-installations-not-naval.html): The burner in its Aegis housing is scoped to fixed defense installations; naval propulsion is explicitly out of scope for the design as studied.

### Strategic Isotopes for Defense
- [14 MeV Fusion Neutrons](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fusion-neutrons-14mev-overview.html): Each deuterium-tritium fusion releases a 14 MeV neutron; these high-energy neutrons are a tool for materials testing that few other sources can match.
- [14 MeV Fusion vs Fission Neutrons](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/14mev-vs-fission-neutron-comparison.html): Fusion and fission neutrons differ in energy, spectrum, and the damage they cause; each suits different tasks, and neither fully substitutes for the other.
- [A Responsible Dual-Use Posture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/responsible-dual-use-posture-isotopes.html): These isotopes have clear civil and research value alongside strategic uses; Kronos presents them publicly, conservatively, and without weapons detail.
- [A Strategic Isotope Reserve](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/strategic-isotope-reserve-concept.html): A reserve buffers supply against disruption, but for decaying isotopes a reserve is a leaky bucket that only a steady production rate can keep full.
- [Accountancy and Safeguards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-accountancy-and-safeguards.html): Every gram of tritium is measured, tracked, and reconciled against decay, so that inventory records match physical reality within tight limits.
- [Alternatives to Helium-3 and Their Limits](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-alternatives-and-limitations.html): Substitute neutron detectors exist, but they generally trade away efficiency, gamma rejection, or maturity, which is why helium-3 remains sought after.
- [Balancing Helium-3 Production Against Tritium](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-supply-from-breeder-decay-balance.html): Because helium-3 comes from tritium, producing more of one interacts with the other; the breeder must balance tritium supply against helium-3 recovery.
- [Border and Port Screening](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-border-security-screening.html): Neutron screening at borders and ports depends on detector supply; helium-3 availability shapes how widely and densely screening can be deployed.
- [Co-Production of Strategic Isotopes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/co-production-of-strategic-isotopes.html): Producing several isotopes from one linked process shares infrastructure and turns by-products into planned outputs.
- [Decay and the Replenishment Requirement](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-radioactive-decay-replenishment.html): At ~5.5% loss per year, a tritium inventory halves in about 12 years; holding a level means a permanent make-up supply, not a single delivery.
- [Demand Drivers for Defense Isotopes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/defense-isotope-demand-drivers.html): Physics, not procurement cycles, drives demand for these isotopes: decay forces tritium replenishment, screening needs helium-3, and materials programs need neutrons.
- [Detector Deployment Logistics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-detector-deployment-logistics.html): Fielding helium-3 detectors is a logistics problem: gas allocation, tube fabrication, calibration, and sustainment all draw on limited supply.
- [Domestic Helium-3 Production Security](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-domestic-production-security.html): A domestic helium-3 stream reduces dependence on incidental or external supply for detection, screening, and research needs.
- [Domestic Isotope Supply Security](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/domestic-isotope-supply-security-overview.html): The breeder addresses three strategic isotopes at once — tritium, helium-3, and 14 MeV neutrons — as a domestic, sovereign supply platform.
- [Domestic Neutron-Source Availability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-source-availability-domestic.html): Access to neutron sources has tightened as older facilities age; a domestic fusion-neutron source adds sovereign capacity for testing and analysis.
- [Domestic Tritium Supply Security](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-domestic-supply-security.html): A domestic, self-renewing tritium source reduces exposure to concentrated supply and to the physics penalty of any interruption.
- [Extraction and Processing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-extraction-and-processing.html): Bred tritium must be recovered from the blanket, separated from hydrogen isotopes, purified, and accounted for before it becomes a usable product.
- [Flux, Fluence, and Dose Rate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-fluence-and-flux.html): Flux is how fast neutrons arrive; fluence is how many arrive in total; together they set how quickly a material can be tested to a target dose.
- [Fuel-Cycle Self-Sufficiency](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-self-sufficiency-fuel-cycle.html): A deuterium-tritium device must breed as much tritium as it burns; the breeder studies a breeding ratio above one to run its fuel cycle and leave a surplus.
- [Half-Life and Inventory Management](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-half-life-and-inventory-management.html): Managing a tritium inventory means budgeting for continuous decay, processing losses, and lead times so the on-hand level never drifts below requirement.
- [Handling and Containment](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-handling-and-containment.html): Tritium is a permeating, decaying gas; safe handling relies on layered barriers, continuous monitoring, and cleanup systems rather than a single wall.
- [Helium-3 Proportional Counters](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-proportional-counters.html): The proportional counter is the classic helium-3 detector: a pressurized gas tube that turns each neutron capture into a countable, gamma-rejecting pulse.
- [Helium-3 Purity and Separation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-purity-and-isotopic-separation.html): Detector-grade helium-3 must be separated from helium-4 and other gases and verified to specification before it can be used.
- [Helium-3 Supply from the Breeder](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-supply-from-hyperion.html): The breeder co-produces helium-3 on the order of ~1.97 kg/yr, adding a domestic, deliberate source to a market limited by tritium decay.
- [Helium-3 from Tritium Decay](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-from-tritium-decay.html): Every year, about 5.5% of a tritium inventory becomes helium-3; recovering it turns a decay loss into a strategic detection isotope.
- [Helium-3 in Cryogenics and Quantum Research](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-cryogenics-and-quantum.html): Beyond detection, helium-3 enables ultra-low-temperature cryogenics used in quantum and materials research, broadening the demand on a scarce isotope.
- [Helium-3: A Strategic Detection Isotope](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-strategic-overview.html): Helium-3 is a scarce, non-radioactive isotope prized for neutron detection; the breeder co-produces it on the order of ~1.97 kg/yr, partly from tritium decay.
- [Honest Gates on Isotope Production](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotope-production-honest-gates.html): Every isotope claim is bounded by explicit gates: the breeder is a design study, breeding ratio is a lever, and no delivered supply is claimed before FOAK.
- [How Helium-3 Detects Neutrons](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-neutron-detection-principle.html): A helium-3 nucleus captures a neutron and splits into a proton and a triton, producing an electrical pulse a detector can count.
- [Independence from Imports](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotope-supply-independence-imports.html): Domestic co-production reduces reliance on external isotope supply, so national needs are met without depending on decisions made elsewhere.
- [Inventory and Decay Management](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotope-inventory-and-decay-management.html): Managing a mixed inventory of decaying and stable isotopes means tracking each one's physics so the right quantity is available when needed.
- [Isotope Logistics and Transport](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotope-logistics-and-transport.html): Moving strategic isotopes safely is a specialized logistics task; for decaying isotopes, transport time is also inventory lost to decay.
- [Isotope Supply-Chain Vulnerabilities](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotope-supply-chain-vulnerabilities.html): Concentrated production, single processing paths, and fragile transport make isotope supply chains vulnerable; decaying isotopes are the most exposed.
- [Isotopes Decoupled from Electricity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotopes-vs-electricity-decoupling.html): The breeder's strategic value as an isotope source does not depend on achieving net electrical output, which separates its supply case from the net-gain question.
- [Materials Qualification with Fusion Neutrons](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-materials-qualification.html): Qualifying materials for fusion and other demanding environments requires exposing them to a representative neutron spectrum and measuring how they change.
- [Measuring Radiation Damage: dpa](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-damage-dpa-metrics.html): Displacements per atom (dpa) is the common yardstick for radiation damage; it lets exposures from different sources be compared on a physical basis.
- [Neutron Activation Analysis](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-activation-analysis.html): Bombarding a sample with neutrons makes trace elements radioactive; the characteristic radiation they emit reveals composition with high sensitivity.
- [Neutron Detection Physics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-detection-physics.html): Cross-section, moderation, and gas pressure together determine how efficiently a helium-3 detector captures and counts neutrons.
- [Neutron Irradiation Testing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-irradiation-testing-facilities.html): Irradiation testing exposes engineered samples to a controlled neutron field and measures how their properties evolve with accumulated dose.
- [Neutron Radiography and Imaging](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-radiography-and-imaging.html): Neutrons see through metal but are stopped by hydrogen-rich materials, making neutron imaging complementary to X-rays for inspecting hidden components.
- [Open Gate: He-3 Demand Outruns Terrestrial Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/gate-helium3-demand-vs-supply.html): A single commercial D–³He unit would need on the order of 400× the entire domestic helium-3 supply per year — terrestrial He-3 cannot fuel the burner.
- [Production-Rate Scaling: FOAK to NOAK to BOAK](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-production-rate-scaling-noak-boak.html): A single first-of-a-kind machine proves the pathway; production rate grows as later units (NOAK, BOAK) follow, turning a demonstration into a supply.
- [Quality Assurance and Chain of Custody](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotope-quality-assurance-chain-of-custody.html): Strategic isotopes require verified quality and unbroken custody, so that what is delivered is exactly what records say, at the specified grade.
- [Quality and Purity Specifications](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-quality-and-purity-specifications.html): Usable tritium must meet isotopic-purity and contaminant limits; specification, not just quantity, determines whether a product can serve its intended use.
- [Radiation Portal Monitors](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-radiation-portal-monitors.html): Radiation portal monitors screen cargo and vehicles for neutron sources; helium-3 detectors give them the sensitivity and gamma rejection the job requires.
- [Radioisotope Safety and Compliance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/radioisotope-safety-and-compliance.html): Producing and handling strategic isotopes is governed by established radiation-safety practice and regulatory frameworks, applied through layered controls.
- [Redundancy Across a Fleet](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotope-supply-redundancy-fleet.html): Multiple breeder units provide redundancy: no single outage halts isotope supply, and aggregate production rate rises as units are added.
- [Sovereign Isotope Production](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/sovereign-isotope-production.html): Sovereign production means the rate, quality, and schedule of strategic isotopes are under national control rather than external or incidental supply.
- [Standards for Neutron Testing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-testing-standards.html): Trustworthy irradiation data depends on standardized dosimetry, sample preparation, and reporting so results can be compared and relied upon.
- [Storage and Getter Beds](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-storage-and-getter-beds.html): Tritium is commonly stored bound to metal-hydride getter beds, which hold the gas safely and release it on demand while decay continues throughout.
- [Strategic Isotopes: The Defense-Value Summary](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotope-supply-summary-defense-value.html): One domestic breeder platform addresses tritium replenishment, helium-3 detection supply, and 14 MeV neutron testing — a sovereign answer to three physics-driven needs.
- [Structural Materials Testing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/structural-materials-testing.html): Structural materials for extreme environments must be proven against embrittlement, swelling, and property loss under a representative neutron spectrum.
- [Supply and Demand Boundary Conditions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-boundary-conditions-supply-demand.html): Whether a tritium source is a net supplier depends on breeding surplus, internal burn, processing losses, and the external demand it is asked to serve.
- [Supply-Chain Resilience for Tritium](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-supply-chain-resilience.html): Resilience means a tritium supply that survives the loss of any single facility, feedstock, or transport link without letting inventory fall below requirement.
- [The Breeder as an Isotope Platform](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/breeder-as-isotope-platform.html): One breeder produces tritium, helium-3, and 14 MeV neutrons together, so a single machine serves several strategic supply needs at once.
- [The Fusion Neutron Spectrum](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fusion-relevant-neutron-spectrum.html): Fusion neutrons peak near 14 MeV, a harder spectrum than fission produces, which changes how they interact with and damage materials.
- [The Fusion-Materials Irradiation Gap](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fusion-materials-irradiation-gap.html): There has long been no readily available high-flux 14 MeV source, leaving fusion materials qualified largely by surrogate spectra and models.
- [The Helium-3 Shortage](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-shortage-and-supply-gap.html): Demand for neutron detection outran the supply of helium-3 from tritium decay, leaving a persistent gap that domestic co-production could help close.
- [The Isotope Supply Timeline](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotope-supply-timeline-foak-noak.html): Isotope supply from the breeder follows a staged timeline: construction from Q2 2027, FOAK first tritium ~2030, then follow-on units.
- [Transmutation and Gas Production](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-transmutation-effects.html): High-energy neutrons transmute elements and produce helium and hydrogen inside materials, driving damage that lower-energy neutrons largely avoid.
- [Tritium Breeding in the Breeder](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-breeding-in-hyperion.html): The breeder (Hyperion) is studied to breed its own tritium in a lithium blanket, with the tritium breeding ratio treated as a design lever across 1.1, 1.5, and 1.8.
- [Tritium Production Pathways](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-production-pathways-comparison.html): Tritium can be made by neutron irradiation in fission reactors or bred in a fusion blanket; the two routes differ in feedstock, by-products, and infrastructure.
- [Tritium and the National Stockpile](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-national-stockpile-overview.html): Tritium is a short-lived radioactive gas the national stockpile must continually replenish; the breeder (Hyperion) is studied as a domestic make-up source.

### Energy Security & Logistics
- [14 MeV Neutron Supply for Defense](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/14-mev-neutron-supply-for-defense.html): The breeder's stream of 14 MeV fusion neutrons is a domestic capability for materials qualification and detection-relevant work.
- [Aegis Fixed-Installation Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/aegis-fixed-installation-power.html): Aegis is the fixed-installation housing of the burner: a sovereign, on-site power concept for defense sites, not a naval or mobile system.
- [Availability Gap for Defense Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/availability-gap-for-defense-power.html): Defense-grade power has demanding uptime requirements; the burner's design-stage availability is a real gap that must be engineered around.
- [Black Start and Cold Start](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/black-start-and-cold-start.html): Black start is the ability to bring power up from a fully de-energized state without help from the grid, a demanding requirement for any prime source.
- [Blackout Resilience for Critical Facilities](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/blackout-resilience-critical-facilities.html): Critical facilities must ride through grid blackouts without losing their mission; the depth of that ride-through is set by their power architecture.
- [Breeder-Bred Helium-3 Pathway](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/breeder-bred-helium-3-pathway.html): The breeder produces helium-3 directly and through tritium decay, a domestic pathway that matters even though it cannot meet burner-scale demand.
- [Burner Honest Gates for Defense](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/burner-honest-gates-for-defense.html): Four physics gates separate the burner resilience concept from a fielded generator; each is stated as a design-and-simulation finding, not softened.
- [Burner as Resilient Power Source](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/burner-as-resilient-power-source.html): The burner is conceived as a resilient prime-power source: on-site, energy-dense-fueled, and independent of the grid, subject to open physics gates.
- [Continuity of Government and Critical Infrastructure](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/continuity-of-government-critical-infrastructure.html): The most essential civilian functions depend on power; sovereign generation is one way to keep them running when the grid cannot.
- [Cost in Lives of Fuel Convoys](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/cost-in-lives-of-fuel-convoys.html): The true cost of fuel logistics is measured in the people exposed to move it, not in any monetary figure, and that cost scales with consumption.
- [Critical Load Prioritization](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/critical-load-prioritization.html): When power is constrained, resilience depends on shedding non-essential loads to keep the mission-critical ones running.
- [Data-Center National-Security Continuity](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/data-center-national-security-continuity.html): Data centers hosting national-security functions must stay powered continuously; their resilience is a power-architecture problem.
- [Defense Computing and Grid Dependence](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/defense-computing-grid-dependence.html): Defense computing depends on large, continuous power that today comes from a grid whose disruption is a strategic vulnerability.
- [Defense Continuity of Operations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/defense-continuity-of-operations.html): Defense continuity requires that command, control, and critical systems keep power through any disruption, including deliberate attacks on infrastructure.
- [Design-Stage Honesty](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/design-stage-honesty-energy-security.html): Everything in this section describes design-and-simulation studies, not built machines; the honest gates are stated so the analysis can be trusted.
- [Direct Energy Conversion and Resilience](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/direct-energy-conversion-resilience.html): Direct energy conversion turns charged-particle energy into electricity without a full thermal cycle, a feature that suits compact, resilient generation.
- [Disaster Continuity of Operations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/disaster-continuity-of-operations.html): In a disaster the grid and fuel chain are often the first casualties; continuity depends on power that does not rely on either.
- [Distributed vs Centralized Generation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/distributed-vs-centralized-generation.html): Distributing generation across many small sources trades efficiency for resilience; centralizing it does the reverse.
- [Energy Density: Fusion vs Diesel](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/energy-density-fusion-vs-diesel.html): Fusion fuels store orders of magnitude more energy per unit mass than combustion fuels, which is the physical basis for a shorter logistics tail.
- [Energy Resilience Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/energy-resilience-overview.html): Resilience is the ability of a site to keep its critical loads powered through disruption; it is a property of the whole supply chain, not one generator.
- [Energy-Security Glossary](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/energy-security-glossary.html): Key terms used across this section, defined plainly: from logistics tail and islanding to availability, breeding ratio, and the burner gates.
- [Fuel Resupply as an Attack Surface](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fuel-resupply-attack-surface.html): Every link that must be replenished is a surface an adversary can attack; reducing replenishment shrinks that surface.
- [Fuel Storage Footprint Reduction](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fuel-storage-footprint-reduction.html): Energy-dense fuel shrinks the storage footprint at a site, reducing a physical, targetable, and hazardous part of the installation.
- [Fusion vs Diesel Generators](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fusion-vs-diesel-generators.html): Diesel generators are proven and available today; fusion offers vastly denser fuel but is not yet built, so the comparison is honest about maturity.
- [Fusion vs Nuclear Microreactors](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fusion-vs-nuclear-microreactors.html): Nuclear microreactors are a maturing resilient-power option; fusion differs in fuel, waste, and readiness, and the comparison must stay honest on all three.
- [Gate: Availability vs Tier III](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/gate-availability-vs-tier-iii-defense.html): The burner's design-stage availability of 0.86-0.995 falls 30-100x short of the 0.99982 that hyperscale Tier III facilities expect.
- [Gate: Helium-3 Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/gate-helium3-supply-defense.html): Each commercial burner unit would demand roughly 400x domestic helium-3 supply, so the fuel does not exist at terrestrial scale today.
- [Gate: Plug Coil Stress](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/gate-plug-coil-stress-defense.html): The burner's plug magnet is overstressed by roughly 3-3.9x at the design bore, making the machine infeasible as specified until the magnet is solved.
- [Gate: Plug Operating Regime](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/gate-plug-regime-defense.html): The burner's plug operating regime lies 166-830x beyond any device ever built, so its behavior cannot be validated against experience today.
- [Grid-Independent Operations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/grid-independent-operations.html): A site that can operate without the utility grid removes one of the two largest single points of failure in its power supply.
- [Helium-3 Strategic Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-strategic-supply.html): Helium-3 is scarce and in chronic shortage; the breeder produces it, and the burner consumes it, which frames the whole sovereignty story.
- [Humanitarian and Disaster-Response Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/humanitarian-and-disaster-response-power.html): Relief operations need reliable power exactly where infrastructure has failed; the logistics of powering them mirror the defense case.
- [Isotope Supply Independence from Imports](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotope-supply-independence-from-imports.html): Several strategic isotopes depend on foreign or fragile supply; domestic breeding reduces that dependence and its associated leverage.
- [Isotope Supply-Chain Resilience](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/supply-chain-resilience-isotopes.html): Resilient isotope supply means multiple production routes, managed inventory, and no single point whose loss ends the supply.
- [Last-Mile Fuel Delivery Risk](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/last-mile-fuel-delivery-risk.html): The final leg of fuel delivery concentrates risk because it is the least flexible, most observed, and hardest-to-reroute part of the chain.
- [Logistics Tail and Operational Tempo](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/logistics-tail-and-operational-tempo.html): The size of the logistics tail sets a ceiling on how fast and how far an operation can move, because power demand travels with the force.
- [Long-Duration Power Without Resupply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/long-duration-power-without-resupply.html): The strategic prize of energy-dense fuel is a site that runs for long horizons between resupplies, shrinking exposure and simplifying planning.
- [Lunar Helium-3 Supply Chain](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/lunar-helium-3-supply-chain.html): Because terrestrial helium-3 cannot meet burner-scale fuel demand, the long-horizon supply story depends on lunar helium-3, gated to roughly 2038-40.
- [MetroVolt: Sovereign Compute Power](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/metrovolt-sovereign-compute-power.html): MetroVolt is the data-center housing of the burner: an on-site power concept for compute infrastructure whose availability must meet demanding standards.
- [Microgrids and Islanding](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/microgrid-and-islanding.html): A microgrid can disconnect from the wider grid and run as a self-contained island, keeping critical loads powered when the grid fails.
- [Reducing the Logistics Tail](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/reducing-the-logistics-tail-concept.html): The logistics tail shrinks along three levers: less demand, denser fuel, and longer resupply intervals; fusion acts mainly on the second and third.
- [Redundancy and N+1](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/redundancy-and-n-plus-one.html): Redundancy keeps critical loads powered when a unit fails; N+1 and higher configurations trade added units for tolerance of failures.
- [Siting Fixed Installations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/siting-fixed-installations.html): Where a resilient generator is sited shapes its logistics, exposure, and hazard footprint; energy-dense fuel widens the siting envelope.
- [Sovereign Domestic Energy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/sovereign-domestic-energy-overview.html): Sovereign energy means the fuel, generation, and critical isotopes a nation depends on are produced and controlled domestically, not imported.
- [Sovereign Tritium Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/sovereign-tritium-supply.html): Tritium is scarce, decays continuously, and has essential uses; domestic breeding is a route to a sovereign, replenishable supply.
- [Strategic Isotope Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/strategic-isotope-supply-overview.html): The breeder produces isotopes with defense and national-security value; domestic production of these is a strategic capability in its own right.
- [The Fuel Convoy Problem](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/the-fuel-convoy-problem.html): Moving fuel to where it is consumed concentrates risk onto a predictable, repeated, exposed movement that an adversary can target.
- [The Fuel Logistics Tail](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fuel-logistics-tail-overview.html): Most of the effort behind powering a fixed installation is not generation but the long chain that moves fuel to it, and that chain is a vulnerability.
- [Waste and Byproduct Logistics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/waste-and-byproduct-logistics.html): Every power source produces byproducts that must be handled; the burner's low neutron fraction and the breeder's isotope streams each carry distinct logistics.
- [Water Logistics for Fixed Installations](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/water-logistics-honest.html): Power generation can carry a water demand for cooling; an honest resilience analysis counts water logistics alongside fuel logistics.
- [Why Breeder and Burner Straddle Defense](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/why-breeder-and-burner-straddle-defense.html): Kronos serves defense from two directions at once: the breeder as a strategic-isotope platform and the burner as a resilient on-site generator.

### National-Security Applications
- [14 MeV Neutron Services: Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-services-overview.html): The breeder (Hyperion) produces a stream of 14 MeV fusion neutrons that can irradiate materials and electronics for national-security-relevant qualification.
- [Accelerated Materials Qualification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/accelerated-materials-qualification.html): A steady, high-energy neutron source lets materials reach lifetime-equivalent damage in a controlled campaign rather than through years of in-service uncertainty.
- [Atmospheric Neutron SEE and Avionics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/atmospheric-neutron-see.html): Cosmic rays create a neutron flux in the atmosphere that upsets airborne and high-altitude electronics; ground testing reproduces that hazard.
- [Border and Port Radiation Screening](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/border-and-port-security.html): High-throughput points of entry screen enormous volumes of cargo for radioactive material; capable neutron detection keeps that screening effective.
- [Detecting Special Nuclear Material](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/special-nuclear-material-detection.html): Detecting special nuclear material relies on catching faint gamma and neutron signatures; efficient neutron detection improves the odds.
- [Displacement Damage and DPA](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/displacement-damage-dpa.html): Displacements per atom (dpa) is the common currency for radiation damage; 14 MeV neutrons accumulate dpa with a damage character specific to fusion.
- [Displacement Damage in Semiconductor Devices](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/displacement-damage-in-devices.html): Beyond single events, neutrons knock atoms loose in semiconductors, degrading carrier lifetime and device performance over a mission.
- [Domestic Supply Resilience](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/domestic-supply-resilience.html): Producing scarce strategic isotopes at home reduces exposure to foreign supply decisions and single-point failures.
- [Domestic Tritium Production: Context](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/domestic-tritium-production.html): Sovereign tritium production is limited and specialized; a fusion breeder offers a production pathway that does not depend on fission reactor capacity.
- [First-Wall and Structural Materials Data](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fusion-first-wall-materials.html): The materials facing the plasma take the hardest neutron load; generating their property data is a core neutron service.
- [Flux, Fluence, and Dose Metrics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-flux-and-fluence.html): Flux, fluence, and dose describe how strongly and for how long something is irradiated; clear metrics make neutron service data comparable and defensible.
- [Fusion vs Accelerator Neutron Sources](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fusion-neutron-source-vs-accelerator.html): Accelerator-based sources and fusion sources both make fast neutrons; they differ in spectrum, steadiness, and scale of service.
- [Fusion vs Fission Neutron Environments](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fusion-vs-fission-neutrons.html): Fission and fusion neutrons differ in energy, spectrum shape, and gas production, which makes fusion sources necessary for fusion-relevant qualification.
- [Handheld and Backpack Detectors](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/handheld-detection.html): Portable neutron detectors let field teams screen for radioactive material on the move; their capability depends on efficient detector materials.
- [Helium-3 and Its Alternatives](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/he3-alternatives-comparison.html): The helium-3 shortage drove adoption of alternative neutron detectors; each trades away some capability, which keeps helium-3 valuable where performance matters.
- [Helium-3 as a Strategic Material](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-strategic-material.html): Helium-3 serves detection, low-temperature science, and other missions; its scarcity makes any domestic source strategically significant.
- [Helium-3 for Neutron Detection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-detection-overview.html): Helium-3 is the preferred gas for many neutron detectors; its scarcity has constrained detection programs, and the breeder co-produces it.
- [Helium-3 from Tritium Decay](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/he3-from-tritium-decay.html): Helium-3 is the daughter of tritium; breeding tritium today seeds a helium-3 supply for years afterward.
- [How Helium-3 Neutron Detectors Work](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/he3-neutron-detectors.html): A helium-3 proportional tube converts a captured neutron into a charged-particle pulse, giving efficient, gamma-tolerant neutron counting.
- [Isotope Metrology and Verification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/arms-control-verification.html): Verification depends on precise measurement; the same neutron and isotope tools that serve detection support transparent metrology.
- [Medical Isotope Production: Dual-Use Context](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/medical-isotope-production.html): Some isotopes used in medicine are made by neutron irradiation; the same neutron economy that serves defense can serve health, a benign dual use.
- [National-Security Applications: A Map](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/natsec-applications-index.html): A guide to how the breeder's neutron economy serves national security across isotope supply, detection, and materials and electronics testing.
- [Neutron Coincidence Counting](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-coincidence-counting.html): Coincidence counting distinguishes materials that emit neutrons in bursts from random background, a key safeguards technique that leans on helium-3.
- [Neutron Irradiation for Structural Materials](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-irradiation-for-materials.html): Fusion neutrons let structural alloys be exposed to representative damage so their behavior can be measured before they are committed to service.
- [Neutron Radiography and Imaging](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-radiography.html): Neutrons image materials that X-rays cannot, revealing hidden hydrogen-rich features and defects in dense assemblies.
- [Neutron-Based Cargo Interrogation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/cargo-scanning-neutron.html): Active neutron interrogation can probe cargo for hidden materials by inducing and reading nuclear signatures; it draws on neutron sources and detectors.
- [Neutron-Induced Single-Event Effects](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-induced-see.html): High-energy neutrons cause upsets indirectly through nuclear recoils; a 14 MeV source is a direct way to reproduce this dominant terrestrial failure mode.
- [Nonproliferation and Safeguards Context](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/nuclear-nonproliferation-context.html): Detection and measurement underpin nonproliferation; the isotopes and instruments involved depend on a healthy supply chain.
- [Radiation Portal Monitors](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/rpm-radiation-portal-monitors.html): Radiation portal monitors screen vehicles and cargo for illicit nuclear material; neutron detection is a core channel, and helium-3 has been its workhorse.
- [Radiation-Hardened Electronics Testing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/rad-hard-electronics-testing.html): Systems that must operate through radiation need their electronics characterized and hardened; a domestic neutron source supports that qualification.
- [Refractory Metals Under Fusion Neutrons](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tungsten-and-refractory-testing.html): Tungsten and other refractory metals handle extreme heat but change under neutron bombardment; qualification quantifies that change.
- [Responsible Dual-Use Posture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/dual-use-responsibility.html): Fusion neutron and isotope capabilities have civilian and security uses; Kronos handles that dual-use nature transparently and conservatively.
- [SEE Cross-Sections and Test Standards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/see-cross-section.html): The SEE cross-section, upsets per unit fluence, is the core measurement of a radiation test; standards make it comparable across labs.
- [SEE Mechanisms in Microelectronics](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/see-mechanisms.html): Single-event effects begin when a particle deposits charge in a sensitive volume; understanding the mechanism explains why some devices fail and others tolerate the hit.
- [Scalable On-Demand Neutron Supply](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/why-fusion-neutrons-scalable.html): A fusion breeder produces neutrons whenever it runs, so its output scales with operating machines rather than with a scarce byproduct stream.
- [Scarce Isotope Supply Chains](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/scarce-isotope-supply-chain.html): Several isotopes vital to security and science are produced in small quantities by a few facilities; concentration is itself a vulnerability.
- [Semiconductor Lifetime and Reliability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/semiconductor-lifetime-testing.html): Neutron exposure ages semiconductors in a controlled way, letting mission-lifetime reliability be measured before deployment.
- [Single-Event Effects (SEE): Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/single-event-effects-overview.html): A single energetic particle can flip a bit or damage a device; SEE testing measures how electronics behave under that kind of hit.
- [Soft Errors in Memory and Logic](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/soft-errors-memory.html): Memories and logic are the most upset-prone parts of a system; neutron testing quantifies soft-error rates and validates error correction.
- [Standards for SEE Testing](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/see-test-standards.html): Publicly available consensus standards define how single-event-effects tests are run and reported so results are trusted and portable.
- [Testing Magnet Materials Under Neutrons](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/rebco-magnet-materials-testing.html): High-field superconducting magnets sit near the neutron source; their materials must be qualified against the radiation they will see.
- [The Breeder as a Neutron Foundry](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/breeder-as-neutron-foundry.html): The breeder converts fusion gain into a stream of neutrons and isotopes, functioning as a foundry for the neutron economy rather than a power plant.
- [The Helium-3 Supply Shortage](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/he3-supply-shortage.html): A sudden rise in demand for radiation detectors outran the limited supply of helium-3, constraining programs and driving the search for alternatives.
- [The Isotope Services Model](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/isotope-services-model.html): Kronos treats the breeder as a foundry: it sells neutron flux and isotope output as services, sized to demand rather than to a power rating.
- [The Neutron Economy for Defense](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-economy-for-defense.html): One fusion neutron stream supports several defense-relevant missions at once: strategic isotopes, detection supply, and materials and electronics testing.
- [Total Ionizing Dose vs Single-Event Effects](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/total-ionizing-dose.html): Radiation harms electronics two ways: cumulative dose that shifts device parameters, and single events that flip or destroy; qualification must address both.
- [Transmutation and Activation Products](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/transmutation-and-activation.html): Neutron capture turns one isotope into another; understanding transmutation is essential to both isotope production and safe operation.
- [Tritium Decay and Inventory Management](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-decay-and-inventory.html): Because tritium decays into helium-3, inventories shrink and generate a co-product; managing both is central to any tritium program.
- [Tritium as a Strategic Material](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-strategic-supply.html): Tritium is a scarce, short-lived isotope essential to several national capabilities; a domestic fusion breeder is a candidate production route.
- [What Is Real Today: Design Stage](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/design-stage-honesty.html): Every capability described in these pages is a design and simulation study; being explicit about that is part of a credible national-security posture.
- [Why 14 MeV Neutrons Matter](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fusion-neutron-spectrum.html): D-T fusion emits neutrons at 14.1 MeV, an energy few sources reach; that hard spectrum is what fusion materials and radiation-hardened electronics must be qualified against.

### Readiness, Standards & Dual-Use
- [ASME Pressure and Structural Codes](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/asme-codes.html): The ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code governs the vacuum vessel, cooling, and pressure-retaining structures.
- [Breeder (Hyperion) Readiness Gates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/breeder-readiness-gates.html): The specific gates the breeder must pass, from simulated plasma to a fleet that breeds net tritium.
- [Burner (Aegis / MetroVolt) Readiness Gates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/burner-readiness-gates.html): The gates the D-3He tandem-mirror burner must pass before it can deliver resilient power on site.
- [Catalog of Honest Gates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/honest-gates-catalog.html): A single list of the open questions that stand between the present design and a demonstrated capability.
- [Civilian Primacy](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/civilian-primacy.html): The machines are designed as civilian energy and isotope facilities first; defense value is a derived application.
- [Configuration Management](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/configuration-management.html): Knowing exactly what was built, from what, and to which revision is fundamental to safety and to fleet replication.
- [Cybersecurity Standards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/cybersecurity-standards.html): IEC 62443 and NIST frameworks protect the plant's control and safety systems from digital compromise.
- [Defense Partnership Principles](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/defense-partnership-principles.html): The terms on which Kronos engages defense counterparts: public-first, evidence-based, and firewalled by default.
- [Design-Stage vs Demonstrated](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/design-stage-vs-demonstrated.html): A precise line between what exists as a validated design and what has been shown in operating hardware.
- [Documentation and Traceability](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/documentation-and-traceability.html): Every claim traces to evidence, every component to its records — the audit trail that makes a program credible.
- [Environmental Compliance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/environmental-compliance.html): Water use, activated-material handling, and effluent monitoring are designed to environmental standards from the start.
- [Ethics and Governance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/ethics-and-governance.html): Governance structures keep the program's claims honest and its dual-use decisions accountable.
- [Export-Control Framework](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/export-control-framework.html): Fusion technology intersects export-control regimes; Kronos designs its disclosures to respect them by default.
- [FOAK, NOAK, and BOAK](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/foak-noak-boak.html): Why the build sequence is structured so each unit retires risk for the next, and what that implies for readiness.
- [Failure Modes and Open Questions](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/failure-modes-and-open-questions.html): The known ways each machine could fall short, published so partners can weigh them honestly.
- [Fusion Regulatory Framework](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/fusion-regulatory-framework.html): How a fusion facility is regulated differently from a fission reactor, and the byproduct-material path Kronos pursues.
- [Helium-3 for Detection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/helium-3-detection-role.html): Helium-3 is a premier neutron-detector gas; a domestic fusion source supports security screening and nonproliferation.
- [IAEA and Safeguards Posture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/iaea-safeguards-posture.html): How a fusion isotope facility relates to international safeguards, and Kronos's design-for-transparency stance.
- [IEC 61508 Functional Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/iec-61508-functional-safety.html): Functional-safety standards define how safety-critical protective functions are engineered to a target integrity.
- [IEEE and Electrical / I&C Standards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/ieee-standards.html): IEEE and IEC instrumentation, control, and electrical standards govern how the plant is measured, protected, and powered.
- [ISO 9001 Quality Management](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/iso-9001-quality.html): ISO 9001 provides the general quality-management backbone that complements nuclear-specific assurance.
- [Integration Readiness](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/integration-readiness.html): Integration Readiness Levels measure whether subsystems that each work alone will work together as a plant.
- [Interoperability and Interconnection](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/interoperability-standards.html): Standards for connecting to grids and microgrids let the burner deliver power to an installation predictably.
- [Manufacturing Readiness](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/manufacturing-readiness.html): Manufacturing Readiness Levels ask a separate question: can the design actually be built, repeatably and to spec.
- [Materials Standards and Qualification](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/materials-standards.html): Structural materials must be qualified for the fusion neutron environment against recognized codes and test standards.
- [Milestone Gating](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/milestone-gating.html): Commitments are structured so that each phase must earn evidence before the next phase proceeds.
- [Neutron-Services Safeguards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/neutron-services-safeguards.html): 14 MeV neutron testing serves materials and detection needs under controlled, transparent, civilian terms.
- [Nonproliferation Commitment](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/nonproliferation-commitment.html): Kronos designs and operates so that its capabilities strengthen, rather than strain, the nonproliferation regime.
- [Nuclear Quality Assurance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/nuclear-quality-assurance.html): NQA-1 and ISO 9001 govern how work is planned, controlled, and documented so quality is built in, not inspected in.
- [Occupational Safety](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/occupational-safety.html): Conventional and radiological worker-safety standards apply alongside the plant's nuclear-specific controls.
- [Open Gate: Availability Falls Short of Tier III](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/gate-availability-vs-tier-iii.html): Projected plant availability is ~0.86–0.995; hyperscale Tier III data centers require 0.99982 — a 30–100× gap in downtime the burner cannot yet meet alone.
- [Open Gate: The Plug Coil Is Overstressed as Specified](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/gate-plug-coil-overstressed.html): At the design bore, the burner's high-field plug magnet carries conductor and structural stress ~3–3.9× the allowable limit — as specified, it is not buildable.
- [Open Gate: The Plug Regime Is Beyond Any Device](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/gate-plug-regime-beyond-devices.html): The plug's required operating point sits 166–830× beyond the regime any mirror device has reached — so today it cannot be post-dicted against experiment.
- [Radiation-Protection Standards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/radiation-protection-standards.html): ICRP-based dose limits and the ALARA principle govern worker and public protection at the facility.
- [Readiness Posture: An Overview](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/readiness-overview.html): Kronos states plainly what is designed, what is simulated, and what remains to be demonstrated in hardware.
- [Readiness Review Process](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/readiness-review-process.html): How readiness is assessed on a cadence, by whom, and against what criteria — before any external claim changes.
- [Responsible Disclosure](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/responsible-disclosure.html): A deliberate split between what is published openly and what is held back keeps the program both credible and safe.
- [Responsible Dual-Use Posture](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/dual-use-posture-overview.html): How Kronos serves defense while keeping civilian energy primary and making only conservative, public claims.
- [Safeguards by Design](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/safeguards-by-design.html): Transparency, accountancy, and nonproliferation controls are engineered into the facility, not retrofitted.
- [Simulation vs Experiment](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/simulation-vs-experiment.html): How Kronos uses simulation, what simulation can and cannot certify, and where experiment remains indispensable.
- [Supply-Chain Assurance](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/supply-chain-assurance.html): A defense-grade program needs a traceable, resilient, and secure supply chain for critical components.
- [Surrogates and Extrapolation Risk](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/surrogates-and-extrapolation-risk.html): Fast surrogate models accelerate design but carry a specific risk: confident predictions outside their trained range.
- [Technology Readiness Levels](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/technology-readiness-levels.html): The nine-level TRL scale, and an honest placement of the Kronos machines within it.
- [The Classification Firewall](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/classification-firewall.html): A structural separation ensures public materials never carry classified, controlled, or weapons-relevant content.
- [The Honest Gates](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/gate-honest-index.html): The starkest results from our own design study, published plainly — because finding them in simulation, before building, is the point.
- [The Plug-Density Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/plug-density-gate.html): The burner's tandem-mirror confinement depends on an unproven plasma-density requirement at the plug.
- [The Standards Landscape](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/standards-landscape.html): A map of the codes and standards a fusion facility designs to, and how they fit together.
- [The Tritium-Breeding Gate](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-breeding-gate.html): Why tritium breeding ratio is carried as a lever, and why net breeding in real geometry is an open gate.
- [Timeline to First-of-a-Kind](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/timeline-to-foak.html): The dated milestones from construction start through first tritium, stated without net-gain claims.
- [Tritium Stewardship](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-stewardship.html): Tritium is stockpile-relevant, so Kronos handles it with accountancy and restraint and never discusses weapons design.
- [Tritium-Handling Standards](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/tritium-handling-standards.html): Tritium is a low-energy beta emitter that must be contained, accounted for, and monitored to established practice.
- [Verification and Validation](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/validation-and-verification.html): Verification asks whether the code solves the equations right; validation asks whether the equations describe reality.
- [What Net Gain Actually Means](https://kronosfusionenergy.com/defense/what-net-gain-means.html): Scientific gain, engineering gain, and plant gain are different bars — and Kronos claims none of them in hardware yet.
